items.label: A
items.critique: 'Hello, young [Class]. I surmise...', 'dead or alive', 'despicable scoundrel', an exact '500 in gold!' and an imperative journal line: textbook Nox, down to the leaked unmasked nickname.

items.label: B
items.critique: Shopkeeper aside, 'Well done, lad!', 'filthy paws', '100 in gold!' and 'Bring that gang of Rogues to justice' are Westwood's voice and journal form.

items.label: C
items.critique: 'Worse than the pox!', exclamation stacking, directions 'through the double doors', and the new-title reward fit the Nox conjurer chapter exactly.

items.label: D
items.critique: 'Thieving little creatures!', 'Hmmm... Yes.', teleporter to the next place; the slightly awkward pacing and campaign-advancing payoff are Westwood's.

items.label: E
items.critique: Strong voice ('forty years and never once run. Last week I ran.') but a colon-led catalogue, specific trees, and a first-person narrative journal entry are not Nox's style.

items.label: F
items.critique: Chiasmus ('No kilns, no charcoal; no charcoal, and...'), semicolons, a nicknamed beast and a long third-person journal summary mark a different writer.

items.label: G
items.critique: 'Ooooh, how can this be?' and the clipped, plot-pushing hand-off are Nox; terse and a little clumsy, as some of Westwood's are.

items.label: H
items.critique: Vivid similes ('long as your thumb', 'like [Person] through a purse', 'size of a hen') and the wistful 'I've nothing left to sweeten' are too literary; the journal restates the whole offer.

items.label: I
items.critique: Opening warning with fragments, semicolons, 'fat as a sow', and a reward with no figure; the journal is a reported-speech paragraph, not a Nox imperative.

items.label: J
items.critique: 'You'll laugh, but...', 'I'd forgotten the mill could be quiet' - a quiet, characterful register; same template as E/F/H/I (nicknamed big one, bigger than X, vague pay plus potions).

tells: Journal form: Westwood writes a short imperative ('Bring X to justice.', 'Retrieve the X.'); the new texts write a first-person reported paragraph ('X the woodcutter says... He will pay me to...').
Rewards: Westwood states an exact sum ('500 in gold!', '100 in gold!') or names the gift; the new texts promise vague 'savings', 'a purse', 'what I promised' plus a found item.
Template sameness: every new text has a tradesman, a beast plague, one oversized leader with a folk nickname, and size similes ('size of a cow', 'fat as a sow', 'big as a dog').
Punctuation and rhythm: semicolons, colons and rhetorical fragments in the new texts; exclamation marks, ' -- ', '...' and interjections ('Ho, there!', 'Ooooh', 'Hmmm') in Westwood's.

Register: Westwood's speakers address the player by rank ('young [Class]', 'Brave [Class]', 'lad') and use stock fantasy invective ('savage scum', 'despicable scoundrel'); the new speakers are understated, rural and wistful.
Westwood's thanks advance the campaign (titles, teleporters, next destination); the new thanks close a self-contained village vignette.
